about: Falernum is Barbados’s own cocktail liqueur, made on the island since at least the 18th century; a 1787 Barbados newspaper already lists it among the drinks served at the Barbados Spa. Many Bridgetown merchants once bottled their own, and John D. Taylor’s, a recipe the brand dates to 1890, is the one that survived. Alleyne Arthur adopted the Taylor recipe in place of its own, and when R.L. Seale & Co., the family firm behind Foursquare rum, took over the brand in 1993, it did the same.

Velvet Falernum is a liqueur rather than a spiced rum: a light, sweet base of cane sugar and spirit, infused with lime peel, almonds and cloves. At 11% alcohol it is gentle by design, the classic Barbadian style, softer and less spice-driven than the stronger falernums from modern craft makers. Its revival owes much to Dale DeGroff, who championed falernum in the early 2000s, and to Haus Alpenz, which brought it into wide US distribution in the late 2000s.

Its real home is the tiki canon. Falernum is the quiet ingredient that completes the Zombie, the Jet Pilot and Three Dots and a Dash, and it sweetens the Corn ’n’ Oil, a Barbadian mix of rum, lime and falernum. Expect lime and almond first, then a soft warmth of clove: a background note that rounds out a drink rather than dominating it.
title: John D. Taylor’s Velvet Falernum
